tables.description: Unconditional and conditional relative frequencies of membership in the ten forecast error portfolios, for all four expectations models
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of all four forecast-error variables (earnings time-series Models 1-2 with 20-quarter phi/delta estimation; price-based Models 3-4 with 250-day residual sigma) and correct decile portfolio assignment using prior-quarter cutoffs. Reproducing the persistence pattern (high conditional frequencies for Models 1-2, near-independence for Models 3-4) validates the paper's central 'proxy effect' argument about period-by-period dependence in portfolio classification.
tables.paper_quote: UNCONDITIONAL AND CONDITIONAL RELATIVE FREQUENCIES FOR MEMBERSHIP OF FORECAST ERROR PORTFOLIOS* (L440)

tables.description: NYSE firm size deciles, 1973-1981: average daily security return, average OLS beta, average Scholes-Williams beta
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct CRSP daily data ingestion, correct NYSE-only universe for the companion portfolios, correct size-decile construction (ranking all NYSE firms at the start of each year, decile mean daily returns over the next 12 months), and correct annual market-model beta estimation (OLS and Scholes-Williams). This is the CRSP-only anchor of the replication — it validates the benchmark portfolios used in every CAR computation without depending on Compustat.

tables.description: Cumulative average residuals for ten forecast error portfolios, all observations pooled, windows [-1,0], [-60,0], [+1,+60], all four models
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the complete event-study pipeline: Compustat quarterly earnings with actual S&P announcement dates as day 0, forecast-error models 1-4, decile assignment with prior-quarter cutoffs, abnormal returns as R_i minus the equally-weighted NYSE size-decile return (eq. 15), and CAR aggregation (eq. 18). This is the headline result table — Models 1-2 show monotone post-announcement drift in [+1,+60] (FEP1 = -3.08% to FEP10 = +3.23% for Model 2) while Models 3-4 show none.
tables.paper_quote: CUMULATIVE AVERAGE RESIDUALS FOR FORECAST ERROR PORTFOLIOS: ALL OBSERVATIONS POOLED* (L1395)

tables.description: Cumulative average residuals for forecast error portfolios broken into five NYSE firm size quintiles, Model 2 and Model 4
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct firm-size-quintile classification (NYSE market capitalization at the start of the year of each earnings announcement, quintiles built from the size deciles: I = smallest-to-.20, ..., V = .80-to-largest) and that the size-decile-adjusted abnormal returns are computed within the correct companion portfolio for each quintile. Validates that the Model 2 drift persists across all five quintiles while Model 4 shows none — the raw material for the Table 7 regressions.
tables.paper_quote: CUMULATIVE AVERAGE RESIDUALS FOR FORECAST ERROR PORTFOLIOS$^a$ BREAKDOWN INTO NYSE POPULATION FIRM SIZE QUINTILES$^b$ (L2118)
tables.notes: Partial: the OCR of Table 6 is damaged for Model 2 portfolios 7-10 (row labels shifted, cells missing). Model 2 is transcribed for FEP1-6 (all windows and quintiles, verified against Table 4 pooled averages and the Section 7 text anchors at L2090) plus the Section-7-quoted quintile-I [+1,+60] CARs for FEP7-10; Model 4 is complete (all ten portfolios verified against Table 4 pooled averages).

tables.description: Cross-sectional regressions of portfolio CARs on forecast-error-portfolio (FEP) and firm-size-quintile (FSQ) codings, 50 portfolio observations, all four models and three windows
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct implementation of the eq. 16 regression (CAR_j = alpha + beta1*FEP_j + beta2*FSQ_j) over the 10x5 portfolio CAR matrix from Table 6, including the sign-symmetric FSQ coding (I-V coded 10..6 for FEP1-5 and 1..5 for FEP6-10) and adjusted-R2 reporting. Validates the paper's headline claim: for Model 2 in [+1,+60], FEP coding explains 81% of cross-portfolio CAR variation, FSQ coding 66%, and jointly 85% (collinearity), while Models 3-4 explain ~0%.
tables.paper_quote: REGRESSION STATISTICS FOR CAR $_j$ AS DEPENDENT VARIABLE AND FEP $_j$ AND FSQ $_j$ AS INDEPENDENT VARIABLES* (L2554)
tables.notes: The regression uses the 50 Model-2/4 quintile CARs from Table 6 (and the analogous Model 1/3 CARs, whose quintile breakdown is stated in the paper to give identical inferences: 'The inferences drawn from this table for the post-announcement drifts for Model 2(4) also apply to Model 1(3)', L2090). All four models' regression statistics are targeted.

tables.description: Subperiod stability: number of quarters (of 10/10/12) with negative quarterly CAR in [+1,+60], per FEP and model, for 7401-7602, 7603-7804, 7901-8104
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates temporal stability of the drift: the paper's claim that 'no discernible sub-period behavior is observed' and the time-period explanation fails — Models 1-2 show predominantly negative FEP1-5 counts and predominantly positive-behaving FEP6-10 counts in EVERY subperiod, Models 3-4 show ~50/50 (no drift) in every subperiod. Validates that the result is not a subperiod artifact.
tables.paper_quote: Table 5 presents results for $[+1, +60]$ for three sub-periods: 7401 to 7602 (10 quarters), 7603 to 7804 (10 quarters) and 7901 to 8104 (12 quarters). Table 5 reports the number of quarters in each sub-period for which the CAR in $[+1, +60]$ was negative. (L1776)
tables.notes: Count cells are small integers (0-12) with vintage-sensitive per-quarter CARs; tolerance_pct=100 and the pattern (Models 1-2: FEP1-5 mostly negative-quarter counts well above half in each subperiod, FEP8-10 near zero; Models 3-4: ~half) is the real target.

tables.description: Pooled CARs for all four models with abnormal return u = R_i - R_m (equally-weighted CRSP NYSE+AMEX index, eq. 17) instead of the size-decile benchmark
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the headline result is not an artifact of the size-decile benchmark: under the market-adjusted specification the Models 1-2 drift in [+1,+60] remains (FEP1 = -2.69 ... FEP10 = +3.78 for the paper) and Models 3-4 still show none. Per the paper's footnote, Models 3-4 FE and FEP assignments are ALSO recomputed with market-adjusted residuals for this table (L3029).
tables.paper_quote: Table 8 presents results for the pooled sample previously reported in Table 4 of this paper when (17) is used to estimate abnormal returns. (L3025)

tables.description: Model 2 CARs by FEP x NYSE size quintile under u = R_i - R_m (eq. 17)
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the confound the paper warns about: under market adjustment (no size control) the largest-firm quintile V shows NEGATIVE CARs across all ten FEPs in [-60,0] and [+1,+60] (FEP10 V = -1.98 / -0.78, paper L3027) — the firm-size effect dominates the earnings effect in large firms when the benchmark does not control for size. Validates both the eq. 17 computation and the paper's rationale for preferring the size-decile benchmark.
tables.paper_quote: Table 9 presents results for earnings forecast Model 2 when (17) is used to estimate abnormal returns. Note, for instance, that in both the $[-60,0]$ and $[+1,+60]$ periods, firm size quintile V (.80 market capitalization decile to largest firm) has negative CAR's across all ten forecast error portfolios. (L3027)
